artiest/joseph-jarman.text:
Joseph Jarman (1937 to 2019) was an American jazz musician, composer, poet and Buddhist priest. He was born in Pine Bluff, Arkansas, and grew up in Chicago. At DuSable High School he had drum lessons from Walter Dyett. He switched to saxophone and clarinet when he joined the army, where he played for a year in the band of the 11th Airborne Division. After his discharge in 1958 he met, at Wilson Junior College, the bassist Malachi Favors and the saxophonists Roscoe Mitchell, Henry Threadgill and Anthony Braxton, among others.

Mitchell introduced him to the pianist Muhal Richard Abrams, and in 1961 he took part in Abrams' Experimental Band. In 1965, together with Fred Anderson and Phil Cohran, they founded the Association for the Advancement of Creative Musicians, the AACM. His first records, from 1966 to 1968 on Delmark, already contained spoken word and small instruments, which later became characteristic of the Art Ensemble of Chicago. He joined that group with Mitchell, Favors, the trumpeter Lester Bowie and later the drummer Don Moye. The group performed in costume, and Jarman wore face paint, a kind of shamanic imagery drawn from various cultures. In 1969 the group moved to Paris, where it lived for years in a commune.

Jarman stayed with the Art Ensemble until 1993, when he left to concentrate on his spiritual life. In 1983 he moved from Chicago to Brooklyn and lived there until his death. On his own albums, such as Song For from 1967 and As If It Were the Seasons from 1968, he shows that jazz can also be poetry, theatre and ritual.
artiest/joseph-jarman.listen: Listen to As If It Were the Seasons and notice the alternation of spoken word, silence and small sounds with expressive saxophone lines.

artiest/joseph-kekuku.text:
Joseph Kekuku (around 1874 to 1932) was a Hawaiian-American musician and the inventor of the steel guitar. He was born in Laie, a village on the north coast of Oahu, in what was then the Kingdom of Hawaii. His exact date of birth is uncertain. At fifteen he went with his cousin to a boarding school in Honolulu. In 1889, at the Kamehameha School for Boys, he discovered the steel guitar technique by chance.

The story goes that he was walking along a road in Honolulu with an old Spanish guitar when he saw a rusty bolt lying there. When he picked it up, the bolt accidentally set a string vibrating and a new, pleasing tone sounded. He practised with the bolt, then with the back of a pocket knife, next with the back of a steel comb and finally with a polished steel bar, as is still used today. In 1904 he left Hawaii for good and performed in vaudeville theatres in the United States with Kekuku's Hawaiian Quintet. In 1919 he went to Europe for eight years with the show The Bird of Paradise, which had begun on Broadway and was well received in Europe.

Afterwards he settled in Chicago, where he ran a successful music school, and later in Dover, New Jersey, where he gave guitar lessons. He died in 1932 of a stroke. In 1993 the Steel Guitar Hall of Fame inducted him as the inventor of the steel guitar, and in 2015 he was given a statue at the Polynesian Cultural Center in Laie. The gliding tone he discovered later became important in country music and in many other genres.
artiest/joseph-kekuku.listen: Listen to a Hawaiian steel guitar in a track from the 1920s or 1930s and notice the gliding tone that moves smoothly from one note to the next, something an ordinary guitar played with the fingers cannot do.

artiest/joseph-koo.text:
Joseph Koo (1931 to 2023) was a composer from Hong Kong, regarded by the Hong Kong Academy for Performing Arts as one of the city's most respected composers. He was born in Guangzhou and moved with his family to Hong Kong in 1948. At seventeen he began piano lessons with a Filipino teacher who also taught his sister, the singer and painter Koo Mei. In the early 1960s Sir Run Run Shaw sent him to the Berklee College of Music in Boston.

After his studies he worked for the film studios Shaw Brothers and Golden Harvest. He wrote the music for the Bruce Lee films Fist of Fury and The Way of the Dragon in 1972. In 1973 he became music director at the broadcaster TVB. From the late 1970s until he moved to Canada in the 1990s, he wrote many well-known theme songs for television series with the lyricist Wong Jim. In 1974, with The Fatal Irony, he wrote the first Cantonese TV theme song, one of the first popular Cantopop songs. His first published song, Dream from 1961, was sung by his sister.

Koo wrote more than twelve hundred songs, many of which are regarded as classics of Cantopop. He received the MBE in 1982 and the Bronze Bauhinia Star from the Hong Kong government in 1998, and won prizes at film festivals. In 2007 he wrote the theme song for The Drive of Life, the series marking ten years of Hong Kong since the handover. In 2012 he gave a concert at the Hong Kong Coliseum, and in 2015 he stopped conducting to take up oil painting, like his sister. He died in 2023 in Canada.
artiest/joseph-koo.listen: Listen to his music for The Way of the Dragon and notice how orchestra and fight scenes work together: the music sets the tempo of the action.

artiest/joseph-kosma.text:
Joseph Kosma (1905 to 1969) was a Hungarian composer who emigrated to France. His best-known piece is the standard Autumn Leaves. He was born as József Kozma in Budapest, into a Jewish family in which his parents taught shorthand and typing. He played piano from the age of five and at eleven wrote his first opera, Christmas in the Trenches. He studied at the music academy of Budapest under Leo Weiner and also with Béla Bartók at the Liszt Academy, with diplomas in composition and conducting. In 1928 he received a scholarship for Berlin, where he got to know Hanns Eisler and Bertolt Brecht.

In 1933 he moved to Paris. There he met the poet Jacques Prévert, who introduced him to the director Jean Renoir. In the 1930s he set poems to music with Prévert, which popular singers recorded and which sometimes became hits. For Renoir he wrote the music for La Grande Illusion, La Bête Humaine and La Règle du jeu. During the German occupation he was under house arrest in the Alpes-Maritimes and was not allowed to compose. Prévert arranged for other composers to serve as a front, and in this way Kosma wrote the pantomime music for Les Enfants du Paradis, which was released in 1945.

From his music for the film Les Portes de la Nuit from 1946 came Les feuilles mortes, with French lyrics by Prévert. In 1950 Johnny Mercer added English words to it and called it Autumn Leaves. The piece appeared in the 1956 film Autumn Leaves with Joan Crawford and became a jazz standard. Kosma wrote for dozens of films, and his melodies are quiet and wistful, with a strong bond with French chanson.
artiest/joseph-kosma.listen: Listen to Les feuilles mortes in the French version and notice how the descending melody and the soft accompaniment translate autumn and farewell into sound.

artiest/joseph-shabalala.text: Joseph Shabalala founded an a cappella group in 1959, which, after a series of dreams, he named Ladysmith Black Mambazo at the end of 1960. Mambazo means axe: the group chopped down the competition in isicathamiya contests. Isicathamiya is soft, creeping choral singing that Zulu workers developed in the cities. Through Paul Simon's album Graceland (1986), for which Shabalala co-wrote the song Homeless, the group became world famous.
artiest/joseph-shabalala.listen: Listen to Unomathemba: the deep basses form a soft carpet, and Shabalala's high lead vocal is answered by the choir each time.

artiest/joseph-szigeti.text:
Joseph Szigeti (1892 to 1973) was a Hungarian violinist. He was born as Joseph Singer into a Jewish family in Budapest. His mother died when he was three, and he grew up with his grandparents in the Carpathian town of Máramaros-Sziget, from which he took his name. The town band consisted almost entirely of his uncles, and at six he received his first violin lessons from his uncle Bernat. As a child prodigy he went to Budapest and was admitted without detours to Jenő Hubay's class at the Liszt Academy.

After his studies he began an international career, at first with salon recitals and virtuoso repertoire. His meeting with the pianist Ferruccio Busoni made his playing far more thoughtful and earned him the nickname The Scholarly Virtuoso. After tuberculosis and a stay in a sanatorium in Switzerland he settled in Geneva, where he became professor of violin in 1917. There he met his wife Wanda Ostrowska and became friends with Béla Bartók. From the 1920s until 1960 he performed worldwide and recorded extensively. His recording of Contrasts with Benny Goodman and Bartók can be found on albums such as Benny Goodman with Arturo Toscanini, Béla Bartók, Joseph Szigeti, Earl Wild.

Szigeti championed new music and many composers dedicated works to him, including Ernest Bloch his Violin Concerto, Bartók his Rhapsody No. 1 and Eugène Ysaÿe his Solo Sonata No. 1. After his farewell from the stage in 1960 he taught and wrote until his death.
artiest/joseph-szigeti.listen: Listen to his recording of Bartók's Contrasts with Benny Goodman and notice the conversation between the clarinet and the violin, which bring classical and jazz-like colours together in a single piece.

artiest/joseph-trapanese.text:
Joseph Trapanese is an American composer, conductor, arranger and music producer, born in 1984. He grew up in Jersey City and studied at the Manhattan School of Music. He works for film, television, records, theatre, concerts and games. His career began with his collaboration with Daft Punk on the soundtrack of the Disney film Tron: Legacy. His arrangements were described as grand and menacing, and the BBC praised the blend of acoustic and electronic instruments.

He then wrote the music for the animated series Tron: Uprising, for the web series The Bannen Way and, with Mike Shinoda of Linkin Park, for The Raid: Redemption from 2012. For The Raid 2 he wrote alone, and for Oblivion with Anthony Gonzalez of M83. He also worked on Straight Outta Compton, The Divergent Series: Insurgent, Only the Brave and, together with John Debney, on the musical film The Greatest Showman. For the drama series Dexter he made the scores for seasons 3 and 4 and the orchestrations for seasons 5 and 6.

His work with artists goes beyond film. In 2015 he wrote string arrangements for the album Compton by Dr. Dre, which he conducted, and for the album Piece by Piece by Kelly Clarkson. In this way he shows how film music and pop music merge in the present day: an orchestra working together with producers, DJs and rappers.
artiest/joseph-trapanese.listen: Listen to the music of The Raid: Redemption and notice the interplay of hard electronic beats and fast rhythms with the driving force of the action scenes.

artiest/josephine-baker.text:
Josephine Baker (1906 to 1975) was an American-born French dancer, singer and actress, and a spy for the French Resistance. She was born as Freda Josephine McDonald in St. Louis, Missouri, the daughter of vaudeville performers. Her career took place mainly in Europe, for the most part in France. In 1927 she was the first Black woman to play the lead in a major film, the French silent film Siren of the Tropics.

In Paris she was a star of the revues of the Folies Bergère. Her performance in Un vent de folie in 1927 caused an uproar. Her costume of a short skirt of artificial bananas and a pearl necklace became a symbol of the Jazz Age and the 1920s. Artists and intellectuals called her the Black Venus and the Creole Goddess. After her marriage to the French industrialist Jean Lion in 1937 she took French nationality. She sang J'ai deux amours, a song about her two loves, her country and Paris. Later came albums such as Encores Américaines from 1951 and Paris mes amours from 1959.

During the Second World War she helped the French Resistance and worked with British and American intelligence, which only became known in 2020, when French documents were made public. She received, among other honours, the Croix de Guerre and was made a knight of the Legion of Honour by Charles de Gaulle. She refused to perform for segregated audiences in the United States and played a role in the civil rights movement. She adopted twelve children, her Rainbow Tribe. In 2021 she became the first Black woman to be inducted into the Panthéon in Paris.
artiest/josephine-baker.listen: Listen to J'ai deux amours and notice her soft, singing voice and the way the lyric turns into a personal declaration of love to Paris.

artiest/josh-wink.text:
Josh Wink, born Joshua Winkelman in 1970, is an American DJ, label owner, producer and remixer from Philadelphia. As a child he learned piano for three years and as a teenager clarinet. At thirteen he became an apprentice to a friend who was a radio and mobile DJ. He taught himself to mix beats and in 1988 met the DJ King Britt, with whom he began making tracks of his own. After turning eighteen he played in nightclubs.

In the early 1990s he was a pioneer of the American rave scene and the best-known representative of the tribal forms of techno and house in the United States. In 1994 he founded his label Ovum Recordings with King Britt. In 1995 he had several hits, including Don't Laugh as Winx, I'm Ready as Size 9, which reached number one on the American Hot Dance Club Play chart, and Higher State of Consciousness, which topped the dance charts in Europe. Later came club hits such as How's Your Evening So Far? and Superfreak (Freak). He remixed Moby, Depeche Mode, Ladytron and Paul Oakenfold, among others.

His style mixes breakbeat, acid house, drum and bass and experimental music. He says that his music is built around tension and that he uses mistakes, by doing things with effects, filters and the sampler that you normally do not do. Rolling Stone described his records as a whirlpool of acid basslines and trippy breakbeats. He names Kraftwerk, Depeche Mode, OMD, early hip hop and Chicago house of the late 1980s as influences and is a great advocate of new DJ technology.
artiest/josh-wink.listen: Listen to Higher State of Consciousness and notice the high, twisting acid line that is filtered again and again, and how it ratchets up the tension in the track.

artiest/joshua-redman.text:
Joshua Redman is an American jazz saxophonist and composer, born in 1969 in Berkeley, California. His father is the jazz saxophonist Dewey Redman; his mother was a dancer and librarian. At the Center for World Music in Berkeley he came into contact with many kinds of music at an early age. He began on clarinet at the age of nine and a year later switched to tenor saxophone, which became his main instrument. He calls himself self-taught and named John Coltrane, Ornette Coleman, Cannonball Adderley and his father as influences, but also The Beatles, Aretha Franklin, Prince and Led Zeppelin.

In 1991 he graduated with distinction in social sciences from Harvard, and he had already been admitted to Yale Law School. He postponed that and moved into a house in Brooklyn, where he landed straight away in the New York jazz scene. He played with Brad Mehldau, Roy Hargrove, Christian McBride, Pat Metheny and Charlie Haden, among others. In 1991 he won the Thelonious Monk International Jazz Saxophone Competition. His first album, Joshua Redman, was released in 1993 on Warner Bros. and received a Grammy nomination.

His playing has a warm, supple tone and a great feeling for melody and swing. He brings together the tradition of Coltrane and his father with influences from pop and soul, and in the 1990s became the face of a new generation of jazz musicians. In doing so he showed that young listeners could find something worthwhile in jazz too.
artiest/joshua-redman.listen: Listen to Jig-a-Jug and notice the tenor saxophone: how does Redman play the melody with plenty of swing, and how do the other musicians react live to his improvisation?

artiest/joshua-rifkin.text:
Joshua Rifkin, born in 1944, is an American conductor, pianist and musicologist. He studied at the Juilliard School and at Princeton University, among other places, and is a professor of music at Boston University. In the classical world he is known above all for his research on Johann Sebastian Bach. He argued that Bach's choral works were sung in the composer's time with one singer to a part. When he proposed that idea in 1981, it was rejected by many colleagues. Later it became very influential, although there is still no consensus. He also discovered that the St Matthew Passion was first heard in 1727 and not in 1729, as had been thought.

The general public knows Rifkin for something quite different. In November 1970 he released Scott Joplin: Piano Rags on the classical label Nonesuch, followed by two sequels in 1972 and 1974. Those records were a great success and are regarded as the start of the ragtime revival of the 1970s. With it, Nonesuch had its first million-seller. Joplin's music thus found an audience again, also outside the concert hall.

Rifkin also moved in the pop music of the 1960s. He wrote arrangements for Judy Collins on the albums In My Life and Wildflowers and played in the Even Dozen Jug Band. With The Baroque Beatles Book he made a witty record on which songs by Lennon and McCartney sound as if Bach or a contemporary had written them. In this way he connected early music with pop, ragtime and folk.
artiest/joshua-rifkin.listen: Listen to one of Scott Joplin's Piano Rags as performed by Rifkin. Notice how the left hand plays a steady, marching beat while the right hand keeps playing just ahead of or behind it.

artiest/josquin-des-prez.text: Josquin des Prez came from northern France and worked in Milan, in the papal chapel in Rome and at the court of Ferrara, before settling in Condé-sur-l'Escaut. He made all the voices equal and had them imitate one another, so that the text remained clear to follow. His motet Ave Maria virgo serena opens with exactly such a series of entries, voice after voice. Thanks to the new music printing, he became the first composer with true European fame.
artiest/josquin-des-prez.listen: Listen to the beginning and count how the words Ave Maria are taken up by the voices one by one, from high to low.

artiest/josylvio.text:
Josylvio is the stage name of Joost Dowib, a Dutch rapper born in 1992 in Naarden. His mother is Dutch, his father Egyptian. He began in 2015 under the name Jaybay and made himself heard that year in a Zonamo session. That same year the single Le7nesh with Sevn Alias was released. The track gave him the chance to make a debut album.

That album is called Ma3seb and came out in 2016. Josylvio made it together with the hip hop producer Esko, a friend from his youth. It reached number five in the Album Top 100 and earned a nomination for an Edison. In 2017 2 Gezichten followed. He also contributed to All Eyez on Us, a joint album by Dutch rappers as a tribute to Tupac, a hero from his youth. His third album Hella Cash (2018), the fourth Gimma (2019) and the fifth Abu Omar (2021) all three reached the top of the Dutch album chart.

Josylvio collaborated often with other Dutch rappers, such as Ali B, Hef, Adje and Jairzinho. He is thereby one of the faces of Dutch hip hop of the 2010s and 2020s. In 2018 he took part in the television programme Expeditie Robinson, which he left voluntarily. His music shows how quickly Dutch-language rap gained a permanent place in the charts.
artiest/josylvio.listen: Listen to Le7nesh by Josylvio and Sevn Alias. Notice how the two rappers alternate and how the beat leaves room for the voices.

artiest/journey.text:
Journey is an American rock band founded in 1973 in San Francisco by former members of Santana, the Steve Miller Band and Frumious Bandersnatch. The group was initially intended as a backing band for other artists, with the guitarist Neal Schon and the keyboardist and singer Gregg Rolie from Santana. Before long the band was playing its own music, at first jazz fusion and progressive rock. A roadie came up with the name Journey.

The first three albums sold modestly, and the record company asked for a more accessible sound and a real frontman. In 1977 the singer Steve Perry joined. With the producer Roy Thomas Baker, who had also worked with Queen, the band made Infinity (1978), with layered vocals and pop-style arrangements. Evolution (1979) and Departure (1980) followed. When the keyboardist Jonathan Cain replaced Rolie, synthesizers took the place of the organ. Escape (1981) became the most successful album, with Open Arms and Don't Stop Believin'. Frontiers (1983) was almost as successful. Later the band continued with other singers, since 2007 with Arnel Pineda.

Journey became the model of what in America is called arena rock: big, glossy rock for stadiums, with powerful vocals, guitar solos and singalong choruses. Critics sometimes found it too commercial, but the audience stayed loyal. Don't Stop Believin' grew into the best-selling digital track in the history of the United States.
artiest/journey.listen: Listen to Don't Stop Believin' (1981). Notice the piano part at the beginning, which keeps repeating the same chords, and how the chorus only arrives at the very end of the song.

artiest/joy-division.text:
Joy Division was formed in 1976 in Salford, near Manchester, after Bernard Sumner and Peter Hook had seen a Sex Pistols concert. The line-up was Ian Curtis (vocals), Sumner (guitar and keyboards), Hook (bass) and Stephen Morris (drums). The group first played as Warsaw and from early 1978 was called Joy Division. Joy Division is one of the bands that turned punk into post-punk: the same do-it-yourself attitude, but slower, darker and with more space.

The band signed to Factory Records, Tony Wilson's Manchester label, and worked with the producer Martin Hannett. Unknown Pleasures was released in June 1979. Hannett had each part of the drum kit recorded separately, so that the drums sound dry and almost mechanical, and used digital delays and echoes. Hook plays his bass high up the neck, so that the bass often carries the melody. The band was not happy with the result: Sumner felt that Hannett had turned the guitars down. Peter Saville's sleeve, with the radio signals of a pulsar, later became a famous image. In 1980 came Closer and the single Love Will Tear Us Apart, which reached number 13 in England.

Curtis suffered from depression and epilepsy. On 18 May 1980, on the eve of the first American tour, he took his own life. He was 23. The other three continued as New Order and, with drum machines and synthesizers, sought out the dance floor. Joy Division influenced later post-punk, gothic rock and alternative rock. In 2026 Joy Division and New Order were inducted together into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame.
artiest/joy-division.listen: In She's Lost Control (1979) the drums of Stephen Morris sound dry and mechanical, because Hannett recorded each part of the kit separately. Listen to Peter Hook's bass: it plays high and carries the melody, while the guitar mainly adds colour.

artiest/juan-atkins.text:
Juan Atkins is an American producer and DJ from Detroit, born in 1962. His father was a concert promoter. As a boy he played guitar and bass in funk bands with friends. After his parents' divorce he moved to Belleville, a suburb of Detroit. There he got to know Derrick May and Kevin Saunderson, and at fifteen he bought his first synthesizer. He listened to Parliament and Funkadelic, to the radio shows of the DJ The Electrifying Mojo and to Kraftwerk.

In 1980 Atkins founded the group Cybotron with the older Richard Davis, a Vietnam veteran with a great deal of knowledge about synthesizers. Their track Clear was released in the early 1980s and is often seen as the earliest forerunner of techno. In 1985 the duo split up. Atkins started the label Metroplex and continued alone as Model 500. With No UFO's (1985) he sold thousands of records, and the style he himself called techno. Later he worked a lot in Berlin, including with Moritz von Oswald in 3MB (1992) and Borderland (2013).

Atkins is called the godfather of techno. He combined the cosmic funk of Parliament with the tight computer pop of Kraftwerk and ideas about the future from science fiction. Together with May and Saunderson, the Belleville Three, he made Detroit the city where techno originated, a style of music that then spread across the whole world.
artiest/juan-atkins.listen: Listen to No UFO's (1985) by Model 500. Notice the tight drum machine, the cool synthesizer lines and the electronically distorted voice, which together conjure up a picture of the future.

artiest/juan-d-arienzo.text:
Juan d'Arienzo was an Argentine tango musician, violinist, orchestra leader and composer. He was born in 1900, the son of Italian immigrants, and died in 1976. His first notable performance was in 1919 at the Nacional theatre in Buenos Aires, during a comic play. Later he took Osvaldo Fresedo's place in a cabaret. There he was given the nickname El Rey del Compás, the king of the beat, by Príncipe Cubano.

D'Arienzo began with traditional tango, but played increasingly modern arrangements. In 1935 he renewed the Argentine tango by stressing both the first and the third beat in four-four time. The result sounds rhythmic and staccato, with a great deal of energy. He himself said that tango consists of three things: rhythm, impact and nuances, and that an orchestra above all had to have life. His orchestra existed for more than fifty years. He recorded more than a thousand tangos, milongas and fast waltzes, often with one of the many singers who worked with him, including Alberto Echagüe and Héctor Mauré. He also appeared in a number of films.

His recordings remain important for dancers. In the milongas of Buenos Aires his music is still played a great deal, precisely because of its firm, danceable rhythm. In this way he remained one of the defining names in the history of the tango.
artiest/juan-d-arienzo.listen: Listen to a waltz by D'Arienzo, for example El vals de los quince años. Notice the sharp, short accents of the orchestra and how clearly you can count the beat.

artiest/juan-d-arienzo-y-su-orquesta-tip.text:
Juan D'Arienzo was an Argentine tango violinist and orchestra leader, born in Buenos Aires in 1900 and died in 1976. His orchestra was an orquesta típica, the traditional tango ensemble with violins, piano, double bass and at least two bandoneons. The tango itself arose at the end of the nineteenth and the beginning of the twentieth century in Argentina and Uruguay among European immigrants. For a long time it was the music of the port districts, of men in a city with far more men than women.

D'Arienzo caused a furore in the 1930s with a sharp, rhythmic sound. His orchestra played with a clear, stamping pulse and short, staccato notes, which urged the dancers on. It earned him the nickname El Rey del Compás, the king of the beat. With the pianist Rodolfo Biagi that sound became even sharper. He brought the tango back to the dance floor, at a time when the music was also being played as music for listening.

La Cumparsita, a tango by the Uruguayan Gerardo Matos Rodríguez, is the most famous tango in the world and D'Arienzo recorded it in 1937. The performance is full of drive and tension. In this way he is among the voices that brought the tango to a large audience during the golden 1940s. The recordings are still popular with dancers in milongas all over the world. His importance is above all that he made the rhythmic core of the tango visible.
artiest/juan-d-arienzo-y-su-orquesta-tip.listen: Listen to La Cumparsita and notice the rhythm: can you hear the short, sharp strokes of the strings and the bandoneons, and how the melody rises above that fixed pulse?

artiest/juan-luis-guerra.text:
Juan Luis Guerra is a Dominican musician, singer, composer and producer, born in 1957. He first studied philosophy and literature in Santo Domingo, then guitar and music theory at the conservatoire. In 1982 he completed a course in jazz composition at the Berklee College of Music in Boston. Back in the Dominican Republic he founded, with local musicians, the group Juan Luis Guerra y 440. The name refers to the tuning note A440. His first album, Soplando (1984), was based on what he had learned about jazz at Berklee. After that he wrote more and more merengues.

The international breakthrough came with Ojalá Que Llueva Café (1988). Bachata Rosa (1990) became a big hit and earned him his first Grammy, with songs such as Burbujas de amor and Rosalía. On Areíto (1992) he criticised corruption and the high cost of living in Latin America, with El costo de la vida among others. Later came Fogaraté (1994), Ni es lo mismo ni es igual (1998) with Mi PC, and in 2004 the largely Christian album Para Tí.

Guerra combines merengue with bolero, salsa, jazz harmony and many other styles. His bachata is softer and closer to the bolero than the street version, with melodies that love bossa nova. He is seen as someone who made bachata known worldwide. That shows how a Caribbean dance music can be refined, with jazz knowledge, into pop music for a large audience.
artiest/juan-luis-guerra.listen: Listen to Bachata Rosa. Notice the guitar with its clear, plucked rhythm and how the soft melody and the harmony sound almost like bolero and jazz, while you can still dance to it.

artiest/juan-luis-guerra-4-40.text:
Juan Luis Guerra is a Dominican musician, singer, composer and producer, born in 1957. He first studied philosophy and literature in Santo Domingo, then guitar and music theory at the national conservatoire. He then went to the Berklee College of Music in Boston, where he graduated in jazz composition in 1982. Back in the Dominican Republic he formed a band with local musicians.

His first album, Soplando from 1984, was released under the name Juan Luis Guerra y 440. The number refers to the tuning note A440, in Spanish Cuatro Cuarenta. According to Guerra, that first album was based on jazz from his time at Berklee and was not intended as a commercial hit. After that he began writing more merengues. Ojalá Que Llueva Café from 1989 is regarded as one of his most acclaimed songs.

Guerra won 31 Latin Grammys, three Grammys and a Latin Billboard Music Award. In 2010 he won three Latin Grammys, including Album of the Year. He is seen as the one who made bachata known worldwide, although his bachata sounds closer to the bolero and with melodies and harmonies derived from bossa nova. He does not limit himself to one style: merengue, salsa, cumbia, pop, jazz, funk, hip hop and religious music all appear. His lyrics are poetic and socially engaged. He is one of the best-known Latin American artists of recent decades.
artiest/juan-luis-guerra-4-40.listen: Listen to Ojalá Que Llueva Café and notice the combination of a cheerful merengue rhythm with a lyric about poverty and hope. Can you also hear the jazz influence in the harmony?

artiest/judy-collins.text:
Judy Collins is an American singer, born in 1939 in Seattle and raised in Denver. Her father was a blind singer and radio presenter. As a child she received classical piano training from the conductor Antonia Brico, but the songs of Woody Guthrie, Pete Seeger and the folk revival attracted her more. She took up the guitar, moved to Greenwich Village in New York and signed with Elektra Records, the label where she would stay for 35 years. Her debut A Maid of Constant Sorrow (1961) consisted of traditional folk songs.

At first Collins wrote little herself. She sang songs by protest singers such as Tom Paxton, Phil Ochs and Bob Dylan, and she drew attention to writers who were still unknown, such as Leonard Cohen, Randy Newman and Joni Mitchell. On In My Life (1966) she let go of the bare folk guitar: the arranger Joshua Rifkin gave the songs a lush orchestral accompaniment, and alongside folk the album contained work by The Beatles, Jacques Brel and Kurt Weill. Wildflowers (1967) contained Mitchell's Both Sides, Now, which earned her a Grammy. Later came Amazing Grace and Send in the Clowns by Stephen Sondheim, from the album Judith (1975), which became her best-selling record.

Collins stands out for the clarity of her voice and for her broad taste: folk, country, show tunes and pop. In this way she became a bridge between the folk clubs and the general public. Many songs that later became classics were first heard by that public in her performance. Stephen Stills, with whom she had a relationship, wrote Suite: Judy Blue Eyes about her.
artiest/judy-collins.listen: Listen to Both Sides, Now by Judy Collins and notice how clear and calm her voice remains above the accompaniment. Then put Joni Mitchell's own version beside it and hear how the same song sounds different when the writer sings it.

artiest/judy-garland.text:
Judy Garland was born in 1922 as Frances Ethel Gumm in Grand Rapids, Minnesota. Her parents were vaudeville performers and she was on stage by the age of two, together with her two older sisters as The Gumm Sisters. Later the sisters chose the name Garland. In 1935, at thirteen, she signed a contract with Metro-Goldwyn-Mayer. At first she got small parts in ensemble musicals. Her breakthrough came with Dorothy Gale in The Wizard of Oz (1939), which also made her signature song Over the Rainbow famous.

She then played leading roles in MGM musicals such as Meet Me in St. Louis (1944), Easter Parade (1948) and Summer Stock (1950). In A Star Is Born (1954) and Judgment at Nuremberg (1961) she showed that she could handle dramatic roles too, and for both she received an Oscar nomination. She recorded eleven studio albums between 1939 and 1962. With her live record Judy at Carnegie Hall (1961) she became the first woman to win a Grammy for Album of the Year. Her voice was a powerful contralto, which she used in many genres.

Garland struggled with dependence on medication, which damaged her health. She died in 1969, aged 47. Her films and recordings were preserved in the American national archives, and six of her recordings were given a place in the Grammy Hall of Fame. For pop history she is important as the great singer of the classic film musical, who sang and acted in one breath.
artiest/judy-garland.listen: Listen to Over the Rainbow. Notice the big leap at the start of the melody and how her voice begins warm and almost whispering and slowly grows stronger.

artiest/juice-wrld.text:
Juice WRLD was the stage name of Jarad Anthony Higgins, an American rapper, singer and songwriter from Chicago. He was born in 1998, had piano lessons as a child and later played guitar, drums and trumpet. His mother did not let him listen to hip hop. He grew up with rock and pop, via video games such as Tony Hawk's Pro Skater and Guitar Hero. Around the age of fifteen he put his first songs on SoundCloud, at first under the name JuicetheKidd. The name Juice WRLD is derived from the 1992 film Juice.

In 2017 the EP 9 9 9 was released, containing Lucid Dreams. He signed with Lil Bibby and shortly afterwards with Interscope Records. Lucid Dreams was released as a single in 2018 and reached number two on the Billboard Hot 100. His debut album Goodbye & Good Riddance (2018) followed, with All Girls Are the Same, among others. Then came Wrld on Drugs (2018) with Future and Death Race for Love (2019), his first number one on the American album chart.

He became a leading name in emo rap and SoundCloud rap, genres that reached the general public in the mid-2010s. His music combines sung lines with rapping, about sadness, love and addiction. Juice WRLD died on 8 December 2019 of an overdose, aged 21. After his death Legends Never Die (2020) and Fighting Demons (2021) were released, among others, and in 2024 The Party Never Ends.
artiest/juice-wrld.listen: Listen to Lucid Dreams. Notice how he half sings and half raps over a calm, melodic beat, and how the heartache in the lyric sits beside an almost singalong melody.

artiest/julee-cruise.text:
Julee Cruise was an American singer and actress, born in 1956 in Creston, Iowa. She studied French horn at Drake University, worked in theatre in Minneapolis and then moved to New York. There she came into contact with the composer Angelo Badalamenti. In 1985 Badalamenti wrote, for David Lynch's film Blue Velvet, a song in the style of Song to the Siren. The rights to the original had become too expensive. Lynch wrote the lyrics and Badalamenti recommended Cruise, because the song needed an ethereal, ghostly voice. This is how Mysteries of Love came about.

Badalamenti and Lynch then made more songs for her, which appeared on her debut album Floating into the Night (1989). The best known became Falling. An instrumental version became the theme tune of the TV series Twin Peaks, in which she also appeared herself as a singer in a bar. Falling won a Grammy in 1991 for best pop instrumental composition. Later came The Voice of Love (1993), The Art of Being a Girl (2002) and My Secret Life (2011). In the 1990s she also performed with the B-52's, as a stand-in for Cindy Wilson.

Her sound is slow, floating and dreamlike, with a very light voice above synthesizers and a soft orchestra. She made the atmosphere of Lynch's work audible and gave the Twin Peaks music a human voice. Julee Cruise died in 2022.
artiest/julee-cruise.listen: Listen to Falling. Notice the low, slow bass line beneath the synthesizers and how her voice floats above it, without forcing.

artiest/jules-de-corte.text:
Jules de Corte was a Dutch singer, pianist and songwriter. He was born in 1924 in Deurne, the sixth child in a poor family with socialist ideals. As a toddler he was blinded by a medical error. He grew up in an institute for the blind in Grave, where he received organ and piano lessons. He turned out to have so much talent that he could make music his profession. In 1945 he became a professional musician, at first at parties and in dance schools, and from 1946 he was heard regularly on KRO radio.

De Corte wrote an estimated three thousand songs, some poetic and sad, others funny. Well known became De vogels, Ik zou weleens willen weten, Hallo Koning Onbenul and Als je overmorgen oud bent. In 1956 the EPs Levensliedjes, volume 1 and Levensliedjes, Volume II were released. In 1953 he sang the campaign song for Beurzen open, dijken dicht, the fundraising drive after the North Sea flood. For years he toured the theatres with his recital programme, and he worked with Louis van Dijk, Albert Mol and Rita Reys, among others.

De Corte is named, along with Ernst van Altena, as the inventor of the word luisterliedje, the Dutch translation of chanson. His songs were also sung abroad, including by Rudi Carrell and Alice Babs. He received, among other awards, the Louis Davids Prize and an Edison. With Wim Sonneveld and Toon Hermans he belonged to the generation that shaped Dutch song after the war, long before there was Nederpop. He died in 1996 in Eindhoven.
artiest/jules-de-corte.listen: Listen to Ik zou weleens willen weten and notice the simplicity: a voice, a piano and a lyric that does the work. Hear how De Corte pronounces the words clearly, so that you can follow every word.

artiest/jules-munshin.text:
Jules Munshin was an American actor, comedian and singer. He was born in 1915 in New York and began in entertainment right after high school. He performed in the resorts of the Catskills, in vaudeville and as a singer with George Olsen's orchestra. During the Second World War he played in army shows, including a tour in which the boxer Joe Louis also appeared.

His breakthrough came in 1946 on Broadway, in the revue Call Me Mister about soldiers returning to civilian life. The show ran for 734 performances. In 1948 he moved over to film. He appeared in the MGM musicals Easter Parade (1948), Take Me Out to the Ball Game (1949), On the Town (1949) and Silk Stockings (1957). He is best known for On the Town, in which, together with Frank Sinatra and Gene Kelly, he was one of the three sailors spending a day's shore leave in New York. Later he also appeared on the stage in London, in 1958 in the play Brouhaha with Peter Sellers.

Munshin belongs to the generation that shaped the classic Hollywood musical. He was not a singer of hits, but a comic talent who drew the laughs to himself within the ensemble. He died in 1970 of a heart attack, three days before his fifty-fifth birthday.
artiest/jules-munshin.listen: Listen to the sailors' trio in On the Town by Sinatra, Kelly and Munshin. Notice how the three voices alternate and how the jokes lie in the lyrics and in the tempo of the singing.

artiest/julian-casablancas.text:
Julian Casablancas is an American singer and songwriter, born in 1978 in Manhattan. He is the singer and main writer of The Strokes, the band he founded in New York in 1998 with Nick Valensi, Fab Moretti, Albert Hammond Jr. and his childhood friend Nikolai Fraiture. His father was John Casablancas, the founder of the modelling agency Elite; his mother was the Danish model Jeanette Christiansen. The group rehearsed a set of fourteen songs, including Last Nite, The Modern Age and Someday. A demo at the British label Rough Trade led to the first release, via the website of the magazine NME.

The debut album Is This It was received very favourably by the press. It was seen as a record that had to save rock in the new millennium, and the Strokes are regarded as one of the most influential garage rock bands of the early 2000s. Room on Fire (2003) and First Impressions of Earth (2006) followed. After a six-year break came Angles (2011), followed by Comedown Machine (2013). Casablancas wrote the early songs almost entirely alone. Later the work became more of a collaboration by the whole group.

In 2009 he made the solo album Phrazes for the Young and founded the label Cult Records. Since 2014 he has been the singer of the experimental rock band The Voidz, with whom he makes less commercial music. His role in rock history lies mainly with the Strokes, where his singing and songwriting were decisive for the sound.
artiest/julian-casablancas.listen: Listen to Last Nite by The Strokes. Notice how vocals, guitars and drums together form one compact sound in which no single instrument takes up too much space.

artiest/juliette-greco.text:
Juliette Gréco was a French singer and actress. She was born in 1927 in Montpellier. During the war her family was in the Resistance; her mother and sister were deported, and Juliette herself, at sixteen, spent months in prison. In 1945 she ended up in Saint-Germain-des-Prés in Paris, the district of cafés and cellar clubs where writers and philosophers gathered. She knew Jean-Paul Sartre, Albert Camus, Jacques Prévert and Boris Vian, and was nicknamed the muse of existentialism.

In 1949 she began as a cabaret singer at Le Bœuf sur le toit. She sang texts by poets and writers; Si tu t'imagines by Raymond Queneau was one of her first successes, and in 1950 she received a prize for Je hais les dimanches. Later she sang work by Jacques Brel, Charles Aznavour and Serge Gainsbourg, and albums such as Juliette Gréco chante Mac Orlan (1964) and La Femme (1967). One of her best-known chansons became Déshabillez-moi. From the 1970s her pianist and later husband Gérard Jouannest wrote the music. She also acted in films, including Jean Cocteau's Orphée (1950). Her career lasted sixty years and ended with a farewell tour from 2015. She died in 2020.

In chanson, the text is what matters, and Gréco turned every song into a small play. She also gave the Paris Left Bank an image: black clothes, dark hair, the artist as bohemian. That image travelled far. Paul McCartney said that The Beatles' Michelle arose from their fascination with Gréco and the Parisian atmosphere around her.
artiest/juliette-greco.listen: Listen to Déshabillez-moi and notice how Gréco delivers the text: she plays with tempo and emphasis, as if playing a role. Notice also how the accompaniment leaves her voice room.

artiest/june-tyson.text:
June Tyson was an American singer, violinist and dancer who became known as the regular voice of Sun Ra and his Arkestra. She was born in 1936 in Albemarle, North Carolina, and worked in the 1960s as a singer in Harlem. She performed in open-air musicals in Jackie Robinson Park in Manhattan. There, in 1968, she caught the eye of Lem Roebuck, the Arkestra's manager, who introduced her to Sun Ra.

From that moment she stayed with the group until her death in 1992. She was the only woman in the band and sang solos, duets and call-and-response with the rest of the ensemble. Since 1972 she had performed regularly with the Arkestra and she can be heard on most of Sun Ra's records from that period. She also designed the costumes, made choreographies and played violin. When she developed breast cancer and could no longer sing, she kept playing violin. Her husband Richard Wilkerson was part of the crew who handled lighting and sound, and their home in Harlem was a regular address for the band members.

In free jazz and avant-garde jazz, Tyson is thus an important voice. She gave Sun Ra's cosmic theatre a human face and a recognisable sound. The album I Roam the Cosmos (2015) keeps her memory alive.
artiest/june-tyson.listen: Listen to a Sun Ra recording on which June Tyson sings. Notice how her voice rises above the Arkestra like a call and how the band answers.

artiest/jung-jae-il.text: Jung Jae-il (born in 1982 in Seoul) is a multi-instrumentalist who works in both pop and film music. He wrote the music for two films by Bong Joon-ho: Okja (2017) and Gisaengchung (2019). For the latter he wrote pieces in Baroque style, such as The Belt of Faith, a seven-minute orchestral cue accompanying a cunning plan by the poor family. The stately music is at odds with what is happening, and that makes the scene ironic. For the series Ojing-eo geim (2021) he wrote Way Back Then: a childlike tune on recorder and castanets, instruments from the Korean primary school, to the rhythm of a well-known Korean cheering clapping pattern (3-3-7). The simple theme was recognised worldwide.
artiest/jung-jae-il.listen: Notice the contrast between the neat Baroque form or the playful children's tune and the cruel situation on the screen.

artiest/jungle-brothers.text:
The Jungle Brothers are an American hip hop group from New York. The core consists of Michael Small, known as Mike Gee, and Nathaniel Hall, who performs as Afrika Baby Bam. In the early years Sammy B was also part of the group. They belong to the Native Tongues collective, which also includes A Tribe Called Quest and De La Soul. They are regarded as pioneers of the blending of jazz, hip hop and house.

Their debut album Straight Out the Jungle was released in 1988 on the independent label Warlock Records and is regarded as one of the most important records of its time. To the reissue that year was added I'll House You, a club hit for which Can You Party? by Royal House, the alias of Todd Terry, supplied the beat. With that they were the first hip hop group to collaborate with a house DJ. They then signed to Warner Bros. and made Done by the Forces of Nature (1989), which also included What U Waitin' 4. In 1990 they contributed I Get a Kick to the Cole Porter tribute Red Hot + Blue. After a four-year break came J. Beez Wit the Remedy (1993). Later they worked with producers such as Alex Gifford on V.I.P. (1999) and tried big beat.

They showed that hip hop could be much more than one style. The group showed how easily hip hop and dance music flowed into one another.
artiest/jungle-brothers.listen: Listen to I'll House You by Jungle Brothers. Notice how the rap falls over a house beat, and how the beat pulls you into the club.

artiest/junkie-xl.text:
Junkie XL is the stage name of Tom Holkenborg, a Dutch composer, multi-instrumentalist, DJ and producer, born in 1967 in Lichtenvoorde. His mother, a music teacher, taught him to play piano when he was three. At eight he began on drums, at twelve on guitar. He was influenced by Pink Floyd and King Crimson and at fourteen took up the bass guitar. At seventeen he worked in a music shop in Leeuwarden, where he learned to appreciate the combination of electronic and organic sounds.

In 1997 he released his first album under the name Junkie XL, Saturday Teenage Kick. On it he combined heavy breakbeats with rock and psychedelia, with vocals by Patrick Tilon of Urban Dance Squad. He then made Big Sounds of the Drags (1999). In 2002 his remix of Elvis Presley's A Little Less Conversation became a worldwide hit. He comes from trance and worked his way via big beat and electronica to film music.

With Hans Zimmer and his company Remote Control Productions he worked on Batman v Superman: Dawn of Justice. As a composer he made, among others, the music for Mad Max: Fury Road, Deadpool, Tomb Raider, Terminator: Dark Fate, the Sonic the Hedgehog films and Furiosa: A Mad Max Saga. His work shows how the dance culture of the 1990s carries over into the big film score, with a solid, rhythmic and electronic sound.
artiest/junkie-xl.listen: Listen to the remix of A Little Less Conversation. Notice how Elvis's voice stays in place, while a tight, modern dance beat is built around it.

artiest/junkie-xl-tom-holkenborg.text: Tom Holkenborg (born in 1967) became known as the Dutch dance producer Junkie XL. His remix of Elvis Presley's A Little Less Conversation became a worldwide hit in 2002. He then went to work in Hans Zimmer's studio in Los Angeles. His first big score of his own was 300: Rise of an Empire (2014). For Mad Max: Fury Road (2015) he wrote music that thunders along like an engine block: drums, distorted guitars and an orchestra that hardly pauses for breath. In the film a guitarist even plays on a moving truck. For Deadpool (2016) he used synthesizers from the 1980s. He combines dance production with orchestral writing.
artiest/junkie-xl-tom-holkenborg.listen: Notice the unbroken, mechanical rhythms of drums and synthesizers, over which the orchestra plays short, hard motifs.

artiest/justin-bieber.text:
Justin Bieber is a Canadian singer, born in 1994 in London, Ontario, and raised in Stratford. He learned to play piano, drums, guitar and trumpet. In 2007, at the age of twelve, he entered a local singing contest with So Sick by Ne-Yo. His mother put videos of his performances on YouTube, where he gained more and more followers. The manager Scooter Braun clicked on one of those videos by chance, tracked him down and took him to Atlanta. Bieber signed with RBMG, a company of Braun and Usher.

His first EP, My World (2009), made him a teen idol. The debut album My World 2.0 (2010) went to the top of the American album chart, with the single Baby. In doing so he was the youngest male solo artist to manage that in 47 years. Under the Mistletoe (2011) was the first Christmas album by a man to debut straight at number one. Believe (2012) and Journals (2013) followed. With Purpose (2015) his sound changed under the influence of dance. It includes Love Yourself, Sorry and What Do You Mean?, three number one hits on the Billboard Hot 100. In 2017 he sang on Despacito. Changes (2020) and Justice (2021) also debuted at number one.

Bieber kept letting his image and musical style change, and moved through pop, R&B and dance.
artiest/justin-bieber.listen: Listen to Sorry by Justin Bieber. Notice the light, danceable production and how his voice shifts between singing and almost whispering.

artiest/justin-hurwitz.text: Justin Hurwitz (born in 1985) studied at Harvard, where he got to know the director Damien Chazelle. Since then he has written the music for his films. In Whiplash (2014) everything revolves around jazz drumming. In La La Land (2016) he revived the Hollywood musical, with songs that refer to old film musicals and jazz. He won two Oscars with it, for the score and for the song City of Stars. For First Man (2018) he used a theremin, an electronic instrument that you play without touching it. In Babylon (2022) he wrote loud jazz for a big band. Hurwitz builds his scores around a few strong themes that keep returning.
artiest/justin-hurwitz.listen: Notice how one theme keeps coming back, each time in a different instrumentation and mood, from solo piano to full big band.

artiest/jymie-merritt.text:
Jymie Merritt, born James Raleigh Merritt, was an American jazz bassist, bandleader and composer. He was born in 1926 in Philadelphia and died in 2020. His mother gave singing and piano lessons and led a choir. After his military service in the army he worked briefly in his father's real estate business. He was then inspired by a recording of Duke Ellington with the bassist Jimmy Blanton, and after a short flirtation with the clarinet he chose the double bass. He studied with Carl Torello, bassist of the Philadelphia Orchestra.

In the early 1950s he toured with Bull Moose Jackson and from 1955 to 1957 worked with the bluesman B.B. King. In 1957 he moved to New York and joined Art Blakey and the Jazz Messengers, together with Benny Golson, Bobby Timmons and Lee Morgan. He stayed until 1962. That year he founded his own group, the Forerunners, which he led, with interruptions, until his death. Later he played with Chet Baker, Max Roach and Dizzy Gillespie.

Merritt was also a composer. His piece Nommo, recorded on Max Roach's Drums Unlimited (1966), earned him a nomination in the DownBeat critics' poll. Absolutions was on Lee Morgan's Live at the Lighthouse (1970). He is thus an example of a bassist who not only laid the foundation, but also wrote music of his own for the great names of hard bop and the jazz of the 1960s.
artiest/jymie-merritt.listen: Listen to Nommo on Max Roach's Drums Unlimited. Notice the bass line that, together with the drumming, forms the backbone of the piece that Merritt wrote.

artiest/k-r-t-wasitodipuro.text:
K.R.T. Wasitodipuro was one of the most respected players of the Javanese gamelan. He was born in 1909 in Yogyakarta as Wasi Jolodoro and died in 2007. His name changed several times over the course of his life, each time after an honour he received. First he was called Tjokrowasito, later Ki Tjokrowasito. In the 1960s the Paku Alaman palace gave him the name K.R.T. Wasitodipuro. Later he became known as K.P.H. Notoprojo. He grew up in the Paku Alaman palace and began gamelan at five, with his father, who led the palace gamelan.

He played in the gamelan of the court and in well-known groups such as Daya Pradangga. From 1934 he was musical director of the gamelan at the radio station MAVRO, during the occupation at Radio Hosokyoku and afterwards at RRI Yogyakarta. From 1953 he taught abroad. He also taught at Indonesian dance academies and founded a school for vocal music. In 1962 he took over from his father the leadership of the gamelan of Pura Pakualaman. Before that he had lived in Solo for a long time, and as a result the Pakualaman style came to resemble that of Solo more. He was also a composer and played the rebab, a bowed instrument.

In 2004 he received the Nugraha Bhakti Musik Indonesia Award. For world music he is important because he passed the gamelan on to students all over the world, so that the palace repertoire of Java was played outside Indonesia.
artiest/k-r-t-wasitodipuro.listen: Listen to a gamelan piece recorded under his direction. Notice how the metal gongs and metallophones together form a calm, rolling pattern and how the rebab lays a singing line over it.

artiest/kabza-de-small.text:
Kabza de Small is the stage name of Kabelo Petrus Motha, a South African DJ, producer and label owner, born in 1992. He grew up in eMalahleni in Mpumalanga and later moved with his brother to Pretoria. His musical career began in 2009. He signed with Tyrique de Bruyne and in 2016 released his first album, Avenue Sound, on Bestbyfar Records. He then founded a label of his own, PianoHub.

He is a big name in amapiano, a South African variant of house music. His breakthrough came in 2018 with the single Umshove, with the singer Leehleza. In 2019 came Piano Hub, an EP with DJ Maphorisa that went triple platinum in South Africa. Together they form the Scorpion Kings, and at the end of 2019 The Return of Scorpion Kings was released. In 2020 followed his album I Am the King of Amapiano: Sweet & Dust, which went straight to number one in South Africa. That same year he was, according to Spotify, the most streamed South African artist. In 2021 he made the album Rumble in the Jungle with Maphorisa and Tresor.

Kabza de Small received seventeen South African Music Awards and in 2021 was named in the Forbes Africa 30 under 30 and in Rolling Stone. Through him the sound of the South African townships gained a place in global dance music. He shows that a new style from the streets of Pretoria can reach an international audience within a few years.
artiest/kabza-de-small.listen: Listen to Umshove by Kabza de Small. Notice the low, rolling bass and the calm, almost creeping beat that are characteristic of amapiano.
